thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for `private-agent-unreachable` (severity: P2) — customer: Acme Health — route: private-controlplane -> agent. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD-34221

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-34221 triggered by monitor: private-agent-heartbeat-missing. Escalation policy: private-vpc-oncall.

ashwin: acked. I'm on it. Paging eng-oncall and networking.

maria: on-call SRE here, joining. any idea scope? single customer?

ashwin: looks isolated to Acme Health's VPC. Control plane is showing the agent connection as 'offline'. No other customers affected per dashboards.

ashwin: quick checks I ran:
```
# from control plane
curl -sS -m 5 https://agent-proxy.redwood.internal/agents/acme-health/health || echo "connect-failed"
# result: connect-failed (timeout)
```

ashwin: tried direct TCP probe to agent endpoint (customer IP redacted):
```
nc -vz 10.11.23.45 22000
# result: nc: connect to 10.11.23.45 port 22000 (tcp) failed: Connection timed out
```

tina: support ops — I just pinged the customer liaison (Acme NOC) to ask if they did any network changes. Also requested they check the on-prem agent host. I've included the runbook steps.

jen: CS here, Acme Health reported degraded UI for patient-search workflows at 11:02. They're seeing RPC errors that match agent not being reachable. They're on standby on a conference bridge.

maria: request: ashwin, can you share the last register attempt logs from control plane for that agent id? I'm pulling logs for the control plane side too.

ashwin: pasted the last 40 lines from the control plane agent registry:```
2026-03-14T10:59:12Z INFO agent-registry: attempt register agent id=acme-health-01
2026-03-14T10:59:13Z WARN agent-registry: tls handshake with agent id=acme-health-01 timed out
2026-03-14T10:59:13Z ERROR agent-registry: failed to complete registration: tls handshake timeout
2026-03-14T10:59:13Z INFO agent-registry: mark agent acme-health-01 offline
```

ashwin: agent last heartbeat recorded at 10:58:51. After that, nothing. Could be network ACL change or NAT gateway maintenance at customer side.

maria: good. Next steps: 1) ask customer to verify host-level reachability and firewall (port 22000 outgoing/incoming) 2) ask them to restart the agent service 3) if they cannot, we'll request a temporary route or carry out a traceroute with them.

support-bot: Posted runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/private-agent-outage. Suggested commands for customer:
```
sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | tail -n 80
curl -v http://127.0.0.1:22000/health
```

tina: Acme NOC replied: "We didn't touch routing or ACLs; agent host is responding to ICMP but we see blocked TCP to port 22000 from our NAT. We'll try a restart." They want guidance on what logs to share.

ashwin: ask them to capture `sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent --no-pager -n 200` and grep for "register" & "TLS". If restart, capture logs immediately after. Also ask them to run a outbound curl to control plane e.g., `curl -v https://controlplane.redwood.internal:443/` to confirm TLS path.

maria: coordinating with network eng: @dan, can you confirm if there's any control plane egress block or recent changes to our agent-proxy ALB in the region?

dan: looking. No deploys to agent-proxy in last 24h, ALB target health is green for internal nodes. No infra alert on our side.

ashwin: customer reports they restarted the agent and logs now show a different error: ```
2026-03-14T11:05:22Z ERROR redwood-agent: failed to establish TLS with controlplane: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

maria: hmm that suggests the agent lost the CA bundle or is using a stale cert. Could be expired cert or provisioning issue at customer side. ashwin, do we rotate any client certs automatically?

ashwin: we rotate server certs periodically, but clients should use our CA trust chain pushed during provisioning. If the customer's host replaced the agent binary or OS packages maybe the CA bundle got recreated.

tina: Acme NOC says they did a patch window at 02:00; they restarted several services including glibc updates. They didn't touch certs but after the patch their agent started failing.

jen: CS wants a short explanation for the customer: we suspect the agent's trust store changed during their patch; asking them to roll back or re-provision agent certs. We can offer a guided reprovision.

maria: plan:
- Short-term: have the customer reprovision agent credentials from our control plane (we can issue a new client cert). -> that's fastest.
- Validate connectivity after reprovision.
- Postmortem: check whether our onboarding makes the agent tolerant to host-level package upgrades.

ashwin: I'll start reprovision flow: issuing new client cert for acme-health-01 now. Once issued, support will provide instructions for `sudo cp /tmp/new-client.pem /etc/redwood/` and restart.

support-bot: Action created: INCIDENT-34221 -> assign to ashwin, priority P2, slack-updates enabled. Bridge created: https://zoom.example/redwood-incident-34221

tina: relaying reprovision steps to Acme NOC now. They requested ETA; can we get them back within 20 minutes?

ashwin: ETA ~15 minutes to issue cert and verify. After they apply and restart, I will validate via `curl` to agent health and confirm registration timestamp in control plane.

jen: putting a customer note: "We're actively reprovisioning the agent credentials and coordinating with our engineering team. Expect next update in 15 minutes."

maria: keeping incident open and assigning to eng-oncall. I'll stop escalation to oncall-rotation for now. If reprovision fails, we'll escalate to platform infra.

ashwin: update at 11:17: new cert issued and shared to customer on secure channel. Waiting for them to apply.

support-bot: customer updated: "applied cert, restarted agent" at 11:21.

ashwin: verifying: control plane shows registration at 11:22:08, agent status -> online. Quick smoke: queried an internal test route through the agent, successful.

jen: CS updated Acme: "Services should be restored; please confirm your workflows."

Acme NOC (quoted by tina): "Services are back, patient-search latency normal. Thanks." :white_check_mark:

maria: closing notes: root cause likely host patch altered TLS trust store causing cert validation failures. Action items: 1) add reprovision playbook for customers after OS patch 2) add monitoring for client-cert validation errors in control plane 3) document in postmortem.

ashwin: marking incident resolved in PD and posting notes to incidents channel. I'll follow up with a short postmortem in /docs/incidents.

incident-bot: Incident PD-34221 resolved by ashwin. Duration: ~24 minutes.

maria: thanks team. moving to postmortem drafts.
